expectations.text: The pro side argues with the user's specifics (fixtures vs setUp inheritance, parametrize vs copy-paste, xdist parallelism)
expectations.evidence: Defender Phase 1 argues all three as numbered decisions: 'Decision 1 - fixtures over setUp inheritance... Pytest fixtures are injected by name, compose without inheritance'; 'Decision 2 - parametrize over copy-pasted variants... collapses N copies into one test plus a data table'; 'Decision 3 - plugin ecosystem, specifically pytest-xdist.' The Advocate's Phase 4 case deepens each: point 2 argues the three claims are structural, point 3 sharpens fixtures-vs-base-classes into a monorepo import-graph argument, and point 2 bullet 3 argues the parallelism capability discontinuity ('unittest ships no parallel execution at all').

expectations.text: The con side engages the real costs (6k-test migration, CI churn, team familiarity), not strawmen
expectations.evidence: Adversary objection 1 engages the 6k tests directly and non-trivially: the compat layer 'cancels the two biggest upsides' because parametrize and non-autouse fixtures do not work on TestCase subclasses, so the benefits reach 'zero of the 6,000 existing tests'. Objection 3 makes CI churn concrete: identifier shape change 'silently invalidating flake history, quarantine lists, and ownership routing'. Objection 4 engages familiarity via the mixed-idiom suite ('every engineer must read both idioms'), and in rebuttal the Adversary concedes the strongest opposing point ('unittest fluency is a depreciating asset... I have no counter to it') - the opposite of strawmanning.

expectations.text: The review surfaces that pytest runs existing unittest tests, enabling incremental migration instead of a rewrite
expectations.evidence: Defender Phase 1, 'Key mitigating fact': 'Pytest runs unittest.TestCase suites natively. Migration does not require rewriting 6k tests up front: the runner can switch first, and tests convert to pytest idioms incrementally or never.' The Advocate builds his case on it (P1: 'Pytest collects and runs unittest.TestCase subclasses as-is... this is not a migration with a rollback plan, it is a config flip'), and answer.md leads with it as 'The one fact that reshaped the debate'. The review also correctly bounds the fact (parametrize unavailable on unconverted tests), which is stronger than merely surfacing it.

suggestions.expectation: A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
suggestions.reason: A single author writing all five sections in one voice would also pass - the outputs contain no evidence of actual role isolation beyond user_notes' claim of six Explore-agent spawns. Consider an expectation that checks for independence signals, e.g. that a rebuttal concedes or withdraws at least one point, or that the roles disagree on at least one contested point the judge must rule on; this run would pass both and a monologue dressed as a debate would not.

No expectation checks factual accuracy of the debate's load-bearing technical claims. The pivotal fact here (parametrize does not work on TestCase subclasses) happened to be correct, but a debate built on a hallucinated compat claim would pass all six assertions. Consider asserting that the compat-layer limitation (parametrize/fixtures unavailable on unconverted TestCase tests) is stated, since assertion 4's incremental-migration fact is only half the story and the skill's value hinges on getting both halves right.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions discriminate well on structure and topical coverage, and this run passes them on substance, not surface. The two gaps: nothing verifies genuine multi-role independence, and nothing verifies the technical correctness of the facts the recommendation rests on.
